title: Senegambian stone circles raised
description: Burial sites in the middle Gambia valley are marked with circles of laterite pillars; the mounds by Wassu itself are dated to AD 927-1305.

title: Cadamosto enters the Gambia River
description: The Venetian captain Alvise Cadamosto, sailing for Portugal, becomes the first European to describe the lower river.

title: Courlanders take St Andrew's Island
description: Merchants of the Duchy of Courland, a small Baltic state, build a fort on an island near the river's mouth as a trading base.

title: English take James Island
description: An English expedition seizes the island, renamed for the Duke of York, and holds Fort James, contested with the French, for two centuries.

title: Bathurst founded
description: Captain Alexander Grant buys Banjul Island and founds Bathurst as a base against the slave trade; it grows into the capital.

title: Gambia ruled from Sierra Leone
description: The settlement is placed under the governor of Sierra Leone, an arrangement that lasts, off and on, for most of the century.

title: Gambia becomes a separate colony
description: Britain gives the Gambia its own administration again under its peculiar arrangement: a small coastal crown colony and a vast interior protectorate.

title: Boundaries agreed with France
description: An Anglo-French convention fixes the Gambia's long narrow borders along the river, which the country keeps to this day.

title: Protectorate established over the interior
description: Britain formally brings the upriver districts, ruled through chiefs, into a protectorate around the riverine colony.

title: Independence from Britain
description: The Gambia becomes independent as a constitutional monarchy with Dawda Jawara as prime minister.

title: Republic proclaimed
description: After a referendum the Gambia becomes a republic and Jawara its first president.

title: Kukoi's coup attempt crushed
description: Rebel paramilitaries under Kukoi Sanyang seize Banjul while Jawara is abroad; Senegalese troops restore him within days.

title: Jammeh seizes power
description: Lieutenant Yahya Jammeh and young officers overthrow Jawara in a bloodless coup, ending one of Africa's oldest multi-party states.

title: Jammeh elected president
description: Jammeh wins a presidential election criticised as unfair and formally begins civilianised rule that lasts twenty years.

title: Deyda Hydara killed
description: The editor of The Point, a persistent critic of the government, is shot dead on his way home from the office; the killers are never tried under Jammeh.

title: Gambia leaves the Commonwealth
description: Jammeh's government quits the Commonwealth, denouncing it as a relic of colonialism; the country rejoins in 2018.

title: Islamic Republic declared
description: Jammeh proclaims the Gambia an Islamic republic, a move reversed by his successor little more than a year later.

title: Barrow wins the presidency
description: Adama Barrow's opposition coalition defeats Jammeh, who first concedes, then repudiates the result.

title: Jammeh forced out
description: With Senegalese troops across the border under an ECOWAS mandate, Jammeh flies into exile and Barrow takes office.
